text: Plip! The pebble sank right to the bottom.
But that big boat is not sinking at all!
It's much bigger than the pebble, and it floats!
Why do boats float?
Let's find out!
I want to sail! Can I make a boat?
Yes! A boat of your very own!
It's tall and shiny! Let's go launch it!
Ollie, I don't think it's ready yet!
Sorry, Pip. It's your boat. You tell us when.
Oh no. It's tilting...
My boat is no good. Maybe I should stop.
Don't stop! I've got a faster way!
Gus, your faster ways always go wrong.
Not this time! A boat needs to be strong. Strong like a lump of clay!
A lump of clay?
Squeeze it hard, and it's a boat in two seconds!
What if we try it the careful way?
Let's watch Gus try first. Then we ask Gran Mari.
Whoa. Where did my boat go?
Gus, your boat sank!
It didn't sink! It's a submarine! I meant to do that.
Do submarines fall down and stay down?
Mine does. It's the best submarine ever.
But a boat should float on top.
It's not my fault. The water was too deep!
And my boat flipped over. Boats are hard.
We need help. Let's ask Gran Mari.
Well now, a muddy seagull and a gloomy crab. What's all this?
Gran Mari, why do boats float?
Oh, that is a good question, Ollie. Let's find out together.
These are the same foil. I'll squeeze this one into a ball. I'll fold this one into a wide boat.
First, the ball. Watch the water.
The ball sinks!
Now the boat. Same foil, same weight.
The boat floats!
The wide boat pushes a lot of water aside. The water pushes back up and holds it. The small ball pushes only a little, so it sinks.
So my clay needed to be flat and wide?
Well now, what do you think happens next?
If we flatten the clay, it will float!
Too much on one side, and it tips. Not a mistake, just something to learn. So we try again.
Try it at home! Fill a sink with water. Squeeze one piece of foil into a ball. Fold another into a wide boat.
Set them on the water. The ball sinks. The boat floats! Add a few stones, one at a time.
Wait, before we go. I fibbed. My boat sank, and I said it was a submarine.
I'm sorry I said I meant to. I just wanted to be fast.
Thanks for telling us the truth, Gus.
It floats! My lump is a boat after all!
What if it tips again?
Try!
I did it! I tried again, and it floated!
Can I ride along, Pip? You're the captain.
Yes! Hop aboard, first mate.
Time for my Wonder Pocket! Three things we learned.
One. A wide, light boat pushes the water aside and floats.
Two. A small, heavy lump pushes less water and sinks.
Three. If a boat tips over, we can try again.
And one kind thing to try today. Cheer on a friend who tries again.
Bye, everybody! Next time, I'll try the careful way too!
